title: Bridge w/ a slave hangs at "connecting"
line: Connecting a bridge, bond or team created in Plasma's network settings now also brings up its ports, so it no longer hangs at "Connecting".
explanation: Ports added from the bridge editor are saved with "Connect automatically" off and are hidden from the connection list, so NetworkManager only starts them if the bridge has autoconnect-slaves enabled. plasma-nm never set it, and because the General tab rebuilt the connection settings from scratch, every save also reset it to the default (off), even when the user had set it with nmcli as a workaround. The bridge therefore activated without its port and waited forever. New bond, bridge and team connections are now created with autoconnect-slaves enabled, and the editor keeps whatever value the connection already has when saving.

commits.message:
kcms/connections: bring up ports when a bond, bridge or team connects

Ports created in the editor don't autoconnect, and every save reset the
connection's autoconnect-slaves, so connecting a bridge left it stuck. New
bond, bridge and team connections now set it, and edits keep its value.

BUG: 421867

media.caption: Master: a new bridge with an Ethernet port created in the settings is stored with autoconnect-slaves=-1 (default, off) and a port that doesn't autoconnect
Fixed: the same new bridge is stored with autoconnect-slaves=1, so connecting it starts the port
Master: editing a bridge that had autoconnect-slaves=1 (nmcli workaround) and pressing Apply resets it to -1
Fixed: the same edit keeps autoconnect-slaves=1

review.text: This cleanly fixes the root cause in plasma-nm: new bond, bridge, and team connections now enable NetworkManager's autoconnect-slaves so activating the controller also brings up its hidden non-autoconnecting ports, and ConnectionWidget preserves the existing autoconnectSlaves value instead of resetting it to default on every save. Both the widgets KCM and the QML KCM are updated consistently, and the dbusmock verification honestly and clearly demonstrates both new bridge creation and preserving the setting across edits.

reviews.text: This cleanly fixes the root cause in plasma-nm: new bond, bridge, and team connections now enable NetworkManager's autoconnect-slaves so activating the controller also brings up its hidden non-autoconnecting ports, and ConnectionWidget preserves the existing autoconnectSlaves value instead of resetting it to default on every save. Both the widgets KCM and the QML KCM are updated consistently, and the dbusmock verification honestly and clearly demonstrates both new bridge creation and preserving the setting across edits.

The diagnosis is right: plasma-nm creates ports with autoconnect off and never set autoconnect-slaves on the bond/bridge/team, and ConnectionWidget::setting() rebuilt the connection settings so every Apply also reset the nmcli workaround. Defaulting new bond/bridge/team connections to ConnectAllSlaves in both KCMs and carrying the value through ConnectionWidget, like master/slaveType already are, uses NetworkManager's intended mechanism, and the stored-settings shots prove both halves. The actual hang can only be checked against real NetworkManager, which the mock can't do, and the entry says so. Bridges created by older plasma-nm keep the default until recreated or changed with nmcli, a reasonable limit for a fix to how Plasma creates them.
